### Why does ChatGPT give different people different answers?

ChatGPT answers can differ from person to person because it does not work from one fixed script. OpenAI says it can use a person’s memory, an approximate location taken from their IP address, and a web search it may run when a question would benefit from current information. Two people asking the same question can get different answers, so one check from your own account shows what your account sees, not necessarily what a customer sees.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-does-chatgpt-give-different-people-different-answers/
Sources: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt ; https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features

### Who should own your Google Ads and Facebook ad accounts?

The business should own its Google Ads and Facebook ad accounts: set up under a login the owner controls, billed to the business, with at least two administrators from the business at all times. An agency can work in the account at a lower access level, such as Standard in Google Ads or Advertiser at Meta, instead of sharing a password, and the owner can end that access when the work ends.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/who-should-own-your-ad-accounts/
Sources: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9978556 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/155909647811305 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1143109949216644

### What answer options should 'How did you hear about us?' have?

Give customers a short list of plain-language options and sort each one into a lead channel: search, AI answer, social, referral, paid, email, campaign or direct. Split 'Google' into search results, the map listing, an AI answer and an ad, since people often use one word for all four. Add an 'Other' box, make the form version optional, and always ask out loud on calls.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-did-you-hear-about-us-options/

### What should you ask before hiring a web designer?

Before hiring a web designer, ask who will own the domain, the design and the logins; who writes the words and supplies the photos; how the site looks and loads on a phone; where inquiries go and how you will know they arrive; and what happens after launch. Then open sites the designer built on your own phone and judge them by how they work, not only by how they look.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/questions-to-ask-before-hiring-a-web-designer/

### Why do my business calls show up as 'Spam Likely' on customers' phones?

Labels such as 'Spam Likely' come from call-labeling services, which the FCC says some phone companies offer. The FCC also says legitimate callers can be blocked by mistake when their calls resemble unwanted ones. An owner can help by calling only with the person's consent, from a valid number that is really theirs, keeping calls per minute and repeat call-backs low, and leaving a voicemail with one consistent call-back number. The owner cannot control what a customer's carrier or phone shows.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-do-your-business-calls-show-as-spam/
Sources: https://www.fcc.gov/call-blocking ; https://www.fcc.gov/call-authentication

### What does 'direct' traffic mean in your website analytics?

In Google Analytics, direct traffic is the channel for visits that arrive by a saved link or by someone entering your address. Visits can land there for other reasons too, such as a link opened from some apps or email programs, or a customer who heard your name from a person or an AI answer and then typed it. It counts visits, not who became a customer, so your lead records tell you more.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-direct-traffic/
Sources: https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9756891

### Google Ads or Facebook ads: which is better for a service business?

Neither is better for every service business, because they reach people at different moments. Google Ads can put your business in front of someone who is searching for the service right now, which often suits urgent jobs. Facebook ads usually reach people who are scrolling and were not looking, which can suit work that sells on looks and trust. Judge both by jobs won, not by clicks.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/google-ads-or-facebook-ads/
Sources: https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/our-approach/ads-on-search/ ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722080 ; https://www.facebook.com/help/562973647153813

### Are you paying for fake or accidental clicks on your Google Ads?

Google defines invalid clicks as clicks that do not show genuine interest in your business, such as accidental clicks, bots and manual clicks that increase your costs. It says it filters them out of your billing, and gives a credit where appropriate and possible when it finds some later. If you suspect traffic it missed, you can ask Google to investigate the last 60 days. Your own count of calls and jobs is usually the better check.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/are-you-paying-for-fake-ad-clicks/
Sources: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/42995 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/11182074

### How should you answer the phone when a new customer calls?

Answer with the business name, your own name and an offer to help. Capture a name and number first, then three things: what the caller needs, where the job is and when they want it. Ask how they heard about you, agree one clear next step with a time, and send a confirmation text only with the person's consent.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-answer-the-phone-for-a-new-customer/

### What is the difference between a domain, hosting and a website, and how do you find out who hosts yours?

A domain is your web address, hosting is the rented computer space where your site's files are kept, and the website is the pages, words and photos visitors see. A business site usually involves all three, and the business should control each account. To find who hosts yours, check billing records, ask whoever built the site and look at where your domain points. A domain lookup shows registration data, which may not name the host.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/domain-hosting-and-website-difference/
Sources: https://lookup.icann.org/

### What happens if your business domain name expires?

Under ICANN's Expired Registration Recovery Policy, registrars must send at least two reminders before a covered domain name expires and at least one more after it if the name is not renewed or deleted. After expiry the name can stop pointing to your website and email, a registrar may delete it at any time after expiry, subject to other ICANN rules, and a 30-day redemption period can follow deletion. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-happens-if-your-domain-expires/
Sources: https://www.icann.org/en/contracted-parties/consensus-policies/expired-registration-recovery-policy/expired-registration-recovery-policy-21-02-2024-en ; https://www.icann.org/en/contracted-parties/consensus-policies/expired-registration-recovery-policy/expired-registration-recovery-policy-28-02-2013-en

### Why are my business emails going to spam?

Business email usually goes to spam because the receiving service cannot confirm who sent it, or because recipients are marking it as unwanted. Gmail and Yahoo both ask senders to set up email authentication for their sending domain, and both warn against bought lists. Send from your own domain, ask whoever runs your email to confirm authentication is set up, email only people who expect to hear from you, and make unsubscribing easy.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-are-your-business-emails-going-to-spam/
Sources: https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126 ; https://senders.yahooinc.com/best-practices/

### What should your business voicemail greeting say?

A good business voicemail greeting is short and covers four things: who the caller has reached, when you will call back, a faster way to reach you, and what to leave in the message. It usually takes under half a minute to say. Promise only a callback time you can keep, then check voicemail as you would any inbox, so a message left today gets the reply the greeting promised.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-a-business-voicemail-greeting-say/

### Why is my website slow, and does it matter?

A slow website often has a cause an owner can see: large photos or video, too many add-ons, or a hosting plan that is too small. It matters because visitors often leave slow pages. Google's web.dev guide says fast sites engage and retain users better than slow ones, and cites a BBC finding of an additional 10% of users lost for every additional second of load time. Test the pages that matter, then ask your builder what is slowing them.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-is-your-website-slow/
Sources: https://web.dev/learn/performance/why-speed-matters ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/page-experience ; https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/about ; https://pagespeed.web.dev/

### Should you turn on domain privacy for your business domain?

Domain privacy keeps your contact details off the public registration record, and it can be a sensible choice for a business. The catch is who is listed as the owner. ICANN says a privacy service keeps you as the registered holder, with alternative contact details published, while a proxy service makes the provider the registrant of record and licenses use of the domain to you. Keep the business as the registrant, and ask which kind you are buying.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-turn-on-domain-privacy/
Sources: https://www.icann.org/en/contracted-parties/accredited-registrars/privacy-and-proxy-service-providers ; https://www.icann.org/resources/pages/whois-rdds-2023-11-02-en

### What is a bounce rate, and should a service business worry about it?

In Google Analytics, the bounce rate is the percentage of sessions, roughly visits, that were not engaged. A visit counts as engaged if it lasts longer than 10 seconds, has a key event, or has 2 or more page or screen views. A service business should not worry about a high number by itself, because a one-page visit that ends in a call can be a success. Judge pages by the inquiries they bring.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-bounce-rate/
Sources: https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/12195621

### What is a tagged campaign link, and how do you use one?

A tagged campaign link is an ordinary web address with short labels added to the end that say where the link was placed, such as a particular email or ad. When someone clicks it, the labels travel with the visit, so your website's analytics can show which campaign sent them. It shows visits, not customers, so write the campaign on each lead as well.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-tagged-campaign-link/
Sources: https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/10917952

### Should a small business buy an email list?

Usually not. People on a bought list often never asked to hear from you. Google's sender guidelines for Gmail accounts say not to purchase addresses from other companies and not to email people who did not sign up, and they warn that spam reports can lower your domain's reputation. The FTC's CAN-SPAM guide says the law covers all commercial email, and that hiring a company to handle your email marketing does not remove your responsibility. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-buy-an-email-list/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business ; https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126

### Should you send an automatic text when you miss a call?

It can help, but send an automatic text only with the person's consent. Keep it to the missed call, with no offers: say you missed the call and how they will get an answer. Log every missed call as a lead whether or not you text. The FCC's consumer guide says its consent rules cover texts sent with an autodialer. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-text-back-missed-calls-automatically/
Sources: https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/stop-unwanted-robocalls-and-texts

### Can you use AI-generated images on your business website?

As general advice, a generated image is often fine as decoration or illustration if the tool's terms allow business use and you never pass it off as real work, a real team or a real customer. The U.S. Copyright Office's position is that copyright does not extend to purely AI-generated material, so you may not be able to claim copyright in such an image. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-use-ai-generated-images-on-your-website/
Sources: https://www.copyright.gov/ai/Copyright-and-Artificial-Intelligence-Part-2-Copyrightability-Report.pdf ; https://www.copyright.gov/ai/

### What can you do if someone copies your website's words or photos?

Save proof first, then ask the site's owner to remove the copy. If that fails, the U.S. Copyright Office describes a notice-and-takedown route for copyright owners, and Google takes legal removal requests for content on its products. Only a copyright owner, or someone authorized to act for the owner, can send a takedown notice. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-to-do-if-someone-copies-your-website/
Sources: https://www.copyright.gov/dmca/ ; https://www.copyright.gov/512/ ; https://www.copyright.gov/help/faq/faq-protect.html ; https://support.google.com/legal/answer/3110420

### Should you boost a Facebook post or run an ad?

Both are paid ads. Meta describes a boosted post as an ad made from something you already posted, and calls it the simplest way to get a post seen by more people. Ads built in Meta's Ads Manager add more choices, including objectives such as leads. For a service business, boosting often suits getting a strong post seen nearby, and a full ad often suits collecting inquiries. Judge either one by the inquiries and jobs it brings, not by likes.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-boost-a-facebook-post/
Sources: https://www.facebook.com/business/help/317083072148603 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/347839548598012

### Is Nextdoor worth it for a local service business?

Often, yes, for a business that serves homes in a set area. Nextdoor says its free Business Page lets a business post to nearby neighborhoods and collect recommendations from neighbors, and it offers ads as a separate option. In Pew Research Center's 2026 survey, 23% of suburban adults said they ever use Nextdoor, against 15% in cities and 11% in rural areas. Judge it by the inquiries it brings.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-nextdoor-worth-it-for-a-service-business/
Sources: https://business.nextdoor.com/en-us/getting-started/business-page ; https://business.nextdoor.com/en-us/small-business/faves ; https://business.nextdoor.com/en-us/small-business ; https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/social-media/

### Is joining a chamber of commerce worth it for a service business?

It can be, when the members include people who hire your kind of service or businesses that serve the same customers as you. A chamber of commerce is usually a membership group of local businesses, and what it offers varies: events, introductions, a member directory, sometimes sponsorships. Visit as a guest before you join if you can. Judge membership like any channel: record each inquiry that came through a chamber contact as a referral, and count the jobs it brought before you renew.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-joining-a-chamber-of-commerce-worth-it/

### Which social media platforms should a service business be on?

Usually one or two platforms, chosen by where your customers already spend time, rather than a thin presence everywhere. In Pew Research Center's 2026 survey, YouTube and Facebook were the most widely used platforms among U.S. adults and about half used Instagram, while use of Instagram and TikTok was far lower among older adults. Match the platform to the people who hire you, post on a rhythm you can keep, and judge it by inquiries, not followers.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/which-social-media-should-a-service-business-use/
Sources: https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/social-media/

### Should a service business use a local phone number or a toll-free number?

For most local service businesses, a local number is the usual choice, because nearby customers may recognize the area code and its calls usually come from close by. A toll-free number, which FCC rules define as one where the business pays the charges for completed calls, can suit a business that serves callers across many states. Whichever you pick, keep it on an account in the business's name. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/local-number-or-toll-free-number/
Sources: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/47/52.101 ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/47/52.107

### Do accessibility widgets or overlays make a website compliant?

Not on their own, and no tool can promise it. In a January 2025 notice of a proposed settlement, the Federal Trade Commission said its complaint alleged that a seller's claims that its automated accessibility plug-in could make any website meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines were false, misleading or unsubstantiated. Justice Department guidance says automated checkers and overlays can help but need to be used carefully. Fixing barriers in the site itself, checked by people, is the safer path. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-accessibility-widgets-make-a-website-compliant/
Sources: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-06/html/2024-31765.htm ; https://www.ada.gov/resources/web-guidance/

### What does a lead generation company do, and should you pay per lead?

A lead generation company finds people who want a service and passes their details, or their calls, to businesses that provide it, usually for a fee per lead. Paying per lead can work when the leads fit your work, are not sold to several competitors at once, and turn into jobs. Before you sign, ask who else gets each lead, what counts as a billable lead, and whether the customer ends up dealing with you or with the seller.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-lead-generation-company/

### Should you build your own website or pay someone to build it?

Building it yourself on a website builder can be enough when you offer a handful of services, can write plainly about them and have the hours to spare. Paying someone usually makes sense when your time earns more on paid work, the site has to do more than describe you, or a first attempt has stalled. Either way, the site should be clear on a phone, get every inquiry to a person, and sit on a domain your business owns.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-build-your-own-website-or-pay-someone/

### Can you move a website built on Wix or Squarespace to another company?

Usually not as a working site. Wix says a Wix site must run on Wix's servers, and Squarespace exports only some content, in a file made for WordPress. What can move is the domain, which both let you transfer to another provider, your contact list, which both let you export, and copies of your own words and photos, which you can save yourself. Treat a switch as a rebuild somewhere else, and keep the old site live until the new one works.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-move-a-wix-or-squarespace-website/
Sources: https://support.wix.com/en/article/exporting-or-embedding-your-wix-site-elsewhere ; https://support.wix.com/en/article/transferring-your-wix-domain-away-from-wix-2477749 ; https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-contacts-exporting-your-contacts ; https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/206566687-Export-your-site-content ; https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/205814028-Import-to-and-export-from-your-site ; https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/205812338-Transferring-a-domain-away-from-Squarespace

### What are retargeting ads, and are they worth it for a service business?

Retargeting, also called remarketing, shows your ads to people who have already interacted with your business, such as by visiting your website, while they browse or search elsewhere. Google now calls these lists "your data" segments, and Meta builds them as custom audiences. For a service business it tends to suit jobs people compare for days, less so emergencies. Judge it by the inquiries it brings, not by how often the ads are seen.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-are-retargeting-ads/
Sources: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2453998 ; https://support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/143465 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2549063 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/744354708981227 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1055828013359808

### What is a marketing funnel, and does a small service business need one?

A marketing funnel is a way of picturing the steps people take before they contact a business: they notice it, they weigh it up, and some of them get in touch. A local service business often has a short funnel, sometimes a single search and a call, so it rarely needs an elaborate one. What it does need is to know where people drop out between noticing and contacting, and to fix that step first.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-marketing-funnel/

### What do 'organic', 'paid' and 'referral' traffic mean in your website analytics?

In Google Analytics, organic means visits from unpaid links, such as ordinary search results or links on social sites, paid means visits from ads, and referral means visits from links on other websites or apps. These are labels Google's rules give to visits, not to customers. Line them up with your own lead channels with care: a referral visit is a click from another site, while a referral lead is often a person who recommended you.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-do-organic-paid-and-referral-traffic-mean/
Sources: https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9756891

### Why was your Google Ads or Facebook ad account suspended, and how do you appeal?

Google's reasons for suspending an ad account include breaking its policies or terms, billing problems such as an unpaid balance, a chargeback or suspicious payments, and protecting against unauthorized access. Meta says it restricts accounts that break its policies, appear hacked, miss its two-factor requirements or show unusual payment activity. Both offer an appeal or a review. Fix the cause first, then appeal once, with honest detail.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-was-your-ad-account-suspended/
Sources: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9841640 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/975570072950669 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/422289316306981

### What do cost per click, impressions and reach mean in an ad report?

Cost per click is what you are charged when someone clicks your ad; Google says this way of paying is sometimes called pay-per-click. An impression is one showing of your ad, and reach, in Meta's reports, is the number of accounts that saw it at least once. A click counts a tap on the ad, not a visit or a customer. These numbers describe attention. What tells an owner whether ads pay is the cost per inquiry and per job won.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/cost-per-click-impressions-and-reach-explained/
Sources: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/116495 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/14074 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6320 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/31799 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2615875 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/710746785663278 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/675615482516035

### Do door hangers, flyers and direct mail still work for a service business?

They can, when the work is tied to a place: a tight service area, a job neighbors can see, or a seasonal service most homes need. Print reaches homes whether or not anyone is searching, so it tends to build familiarity more than it catches urgent needs. Give each drop its own phone number, short web address or code, ask every new customer how they heard of you, and judge it by jobs won, not by pieces sent.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-door-hangers-flyers-and-direct-mail-work/
Sources: https://www.usps.com/business/every-door-direct-mail.htm

### How do you spot a fake invoice or a payment-change email?

Be wary of any email that asks you to pay a new account, change bank details or rush a payment, even when it seems to come from a supplier or customer you know. The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center calls this business email compromise. Check every payment change by calling a number you already have, not one in the email. If money has already gone, contact your bank at once and file a complaint at ic3.gov.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-spot-a-fake-invoice-or-payment-change-email/
Sources: https://www.ic3.gov/CrimeInfo/BEC ; https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2024/PSA240911

### Why isn't my business showing up on Google?

Usually for a reason you can check. You may have searched your name, while customers search the service and the town. Your site may have no page that names that service and place in plain words. Your Google Business Profile may be missing, unverified or suspended. The site may lose the visitors it gets because it is slow or broken on a phone. Few people may search the words you expect. Or competitors may have more going for them. Check in that order, and beware anyone promising page one.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-is-my-business-not-showing-up-on-google/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### Why are my competitors showing up on Google instead of me?

Usually because Google judges their page a closer fit for what the customer typed, or the business behind it looks better established. Most of the visible differences take about twenty minutes to find: search the way customers do, then compare their page, reviews and profile with yours. Some gaps can close in a quarter; others, such as a long history of reviews, take longer. No outsider can see exactly how Google weighs any of it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-competitors-show-up-on-google-instead-of-you/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### How do I get ChatGPT to recommend my business?

You cannot make ChatGPT recommend you, and you should be wary of anyone who offers to sell you a place inside its written answer. What you control is what it can find: a website that says plainly what you do, where and for whom; the exact services customers ask for, named in their words; honest reviews and mentions on other sites; and facts about your business that are current. Then ask ChatGPT yourself each month and note what it says.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-get-chatgpt-to-recommend-your-business/
Sources: https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/

### How do I get my business mentioned in Google AI Overviews?

By being a plain, complete answer to the questions your customers ask, on a page that can already show up in ordinary Google results. Google says "There are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode", so the route runs through its regular search advice. Search three customer questions today to see whether an Overview appears and who it names, and be wary of anyone who promises you a mention.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-get-mentioned-in-google-ai-overviews/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### My website gets traffic but no customers. Who can fix that?

It depends on where people drop out, so find that first. Look at three stages: visits that never become inquiries, inquiries that arrive but go cold, and inquiries that do not close. The first is the page and its ask, usually fixed by you or a web designer. The second is lead handling: slow replies, missed calls, after-hours gaps. The third is the offer, the price conversation and the fit, which usually rest with the owner.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/website-gets-traffic-but-no-customers/
Sources: https://hbr.org/2011/03/the-short-life-of-online-sales-leads

### How can I generate more leads for my service business?

Pull two levers: get more inquiries, and lose fewer of the ones you already get. Losing fewer usually comes first, since those people already asked: reply fast, follow up, cover after hours, and tag every inquiry with its source so you can repeat what works. For more inquiries, choose among eight channels (search, AI answer, social, referral, paid, email, campaign and direct) by what each takes from you and how soon it tends to pay.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-get-more-leads-for-a-service-business/

### How can I automate my lead generation process?

Automate the steps that are the same every time: an alert to your phone the minute an inquiry lands, a short first reply that says when you will call, a reminder to follow up, the source tag on every inquiry, and a monthly count by source and outcome. Keep the quote, the decision on fit, apologies and anything a customer may quote back in human hands. Send automatic texts or calls only with the person's consent.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-parts-of-lead-generation-can-you-automate/
Sources: https://hbr.org/2011/03/the-short-life-of-online-sales-leads

### Who can help me improve my online presence and attract more clients?

Match the help to the problem. A web designer or developer fixes the site; an SEO or GEO agency or consultant works on being found on Google and named in AI answers; someone who sets up lead handling fixes inquiries that are lost, slow or untracked; a social media manager helps only if customers come from social. Owners can often do much of it alone. Insist that every inquiry is tagged with its source and that you own your domain, content and data.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/who-can-help-improve-your-online-presence/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### How should a business respond to a negative Google review?

Reply briefly and calmly, for the customers who read it later. Google's tips: be polite, apologize when appropriate, admit real mistakes but not things outside your control, never share the reviewer's private information, and, when it is complex, offer to talk by phone or email. The FTC says a business may reply publicly, but its rule bars knowingly or recklessly false accusations about a reviewer, and threats or intimidation to get a review removed or changed. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-respond-to-a-negative-google-review/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474050 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122 ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers

### Why are some of my Google reviews missing or not showing up?

Google says missing reviews were usually removed for breaking its policies, such as spam, and those are not restored. Others are delayed: a new review can take a few days to be checked, and reviews from merged profiles a few days to show. A customer on an older phone may not have managed to post. Google can also pause reviews on some profiles, and its spam filter occasionally removes real ones; for that, contact Google support.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-are-google-reviews-missing/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/10313341 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4596773 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/14114287 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122 ; https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114

### Why is my business not showing up on Google Maps?

Most often the profile itself is the reason, and you can see which from inside it. Google says only verified businesses can show their info on Maps and Search, so an unclaimed or unverified profile may not appear. A suspended profile, or one Google treats as a duplicate, does not show either. A service-area business that hides its address shows only its service area, and Google says rankings for a new business can take up to a month to appear.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-is-your-business-not-showing-on-google-maps/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/145585 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/7107242 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/12756178 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/2853879 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/14271705

### How do you verify a Google Business Profile, and why does Google ask for a video?

Verification is how Google confirms you run the business; until then you cannot edit the profile or interact with customers through it. Google decides which methods you get, based on business type, public info, region or hours: phone or text, email, a live video call, a postcard or a recorded video, which it recommends when you are eligible. The video must show where you are, that the business exists and that you run it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-verify-a-google-business-profile/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/7107242 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/14271705 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474050

### What should you do when Google changes your hours or says your business is closed?

Google updates profiles from user suggestions, licensed content and other sources, so your hours or a closed label can change without you. Info Google changed shows in blue in the profile editor. For some suggested edits Google notifies the owner, who has 4 days to accept or reject; with no response, it may publish the edit if other public information supports it. To fix it, sign in, open Edit profile, then Hours, and correct the hours, or reopen a location marked closed by mistake.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/google-changed-your-hours-or-says-you-are-closed/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3480441 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/15300403 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/6303076 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/15300196 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/15300571 ; https://support.google.com/maps/answer/7084895 ; https://support.google.com/maps/answer/10552932

### Are AEO, GEO and AI SEO the same thing?

Mostly, yes. AEO (answer engine optimization), GEO (generative engine optimization), AI SEO, LLMO and AIO are mostly names for one aim: a business being visible and accurately described in answers written by AI. GEO comes from a 2023 research paper; the other names are used in different ways by vendors and publications, with no agreed definition. Google calls the work still SEO for its own search. What a seller will check and report tells you more than the label.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/are-aeo-geo-and-ai-seo-the-same/
Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735 ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_engine_optimization

### Can you add your business to ChatGPT?

Not in the way you add a business to a map. OpenAI's "Build for ChatGPT" page for developers lists plugins, workspace agents, a shopping connection for merchants and ads. None is described there as a way to be placed in ChatGPT's written answers. A quote-request button for local businesses exists, but only as a beta with approved partners. Whether ChatGPT names you still depends on what it can find about your business.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-add-your-business-to-chatgpt/
Sources: https://developers.openai.com/chatgpt ; https://developers.openai.com/plugins/concepts/plugins ; https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/submission ; https://developers.openai.com/commerce/guides/get-started ; https://developers.openai.com/plugins/guides/local-services-request-quote-conversion-spec

### Where does ChatGPT get its information about a business?

From a few places. In its 2025 system card for GPT-5, OpenAI said those models, like its others, were trained on information publicly available on the internet, information it accesses through partners, and information from users, trainers and researchers. When ChatGPT searches the web, results and their sources appear in the chat. For a quote-request feature in beta, approved partners also supply local business records. That is why a clear, current website and honest mentions elsewhere usually matter to what it says about you.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/where-does-chatgpt-get-its-information/
Sources: https://cdn.openai.com/gpt-5-system-card.pdf ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/web-search ; https://developers.openai.com/plugins/guides/local-services-request-quote-conversion-spec

### Should you hire a marketing employee, a fractional marketing lead or an agency?

It depends on how much work there is, which skills it needs and who will manage it. An employee usually suits steady work that fills a week and that you can direct. A fractional marketing lead, an experienced marketer hired part time, often suits a business that needs a plan and oversight more than extra hands. An agency usually suits work that spans several skills. Whichever you choose, keep the domain, website, ad accounts and lead records in the business's name.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-hire-a-marketing-employee-or-an-agency/
Sources: https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/advertising-promotions-and-marketing-managers.htm

### Can AI tools do your SEO for you?

Partly. An AI tool can help an owner draft pages, list the questions customers ask and tidy wording, but it cannot know the business's real facts, earn honest reviews or mentions, or see which inquiries came from search. Google says appropriate use of AI is not against its guidelines, while using it to churn out many pages without adding value can break its spam policies. Treat AI as help for someone who knows the business, not a replacement.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-ai-do-your-seo/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/02/google-search-and-ai-content ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide

### How do you change your business name or address on Google without losing your reviews?

For a move or a minor rename, edit the profile you already have rather than starting a new one. Google says a business that moves and keeps its name has its reviews transferred automatically, though for some categories, such as hotels, they might not move, and that a minor name change keeps them too. For a bigger rename, Google says to mark the old profile closed and create a new one. Google reviews changes before they go live, and a business that moves after it is verified must verify again.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/change-your-business-name-or-address-on-google/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/2853879 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3098204 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/15300571

### How do you give an employee or agency access to your Google Business Profile without giving up ownership?

Invite them from People and access in your profile's settings, using their own Google Account, and choose Manager rather than Owner. Google says managers have mostly the same access as owners, such as editing info, replying to reviews and posting, but cannot add or remove users or remove the profile. Keep primary ownership yourself, and when someone leaves, remove them from the same screen.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/give-someone-access-to-your-google-business-profile/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3403100 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3415281 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/13763036

### What should you do if someone threatens to post bad reviews unless you pay?

Do not pay, and do not negotiate. Google says these scams may involve a sudden rise in 1-star and 2-star reviews, followed by a demand for money, goods or services to remove them, and that paying can encourage further attempts. Screenshot every message with its date and sender, link each suspect review, and report it on Google's merchant extortion form. The FTC asks businesses to report scams at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-to-do-about-review-extortion/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/16404809 ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/scams-your-small-business-guide-business ; https://www.yelp.com/guidelines

### Is BBB accreditation worth it for a small business?

It can be, if your customers check the Better Business Bureau before they hire, but judge it by the inquiries it brings, not the seal. Accreditation is a paid status: the business affirms it meets the BBB's standards, such as honest advertising and answering complaints the BBB forwards, and needs at least a B rating. The rating is separate: the BBB grades businesses from A+ to F, and says customer reviews are not used in that grade.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-bbb-accreditation-worth-it/
Sources: https://www.bbb.org/business/accreditation/standards ; https://www.bbb.org/about/overview-of-ratings ; https://www.bbb.org/get-listed

### Why does Yelp hide some of my reviews, and can I ask customers to review me there?

Yelp's automated recommendation software decides which reviews to recommend. Reviews it does not recommend, such as ones from less active users, from people with ties to the business, or ones it thinks the business asked for, sit behind a link at the bottom of the page and do not count toward the star rating or review count. No Yelp employee can override it, and unlike Google, Yelp says businesses should never ask customers to write reviews.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-does-yelp-hide-some-reviews/
Sources: https://www.yelp-support.com/article/Why-would-a-review-not-be-recommended?l=en_US ; https://trust.yelp.com/recommendation-software/ ; https://www.yelp-support.com/article/Don-t-Ask-for-Reviews?l=en_US ; https://www.yelp.com/guidelines ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122

### What does a marketing agency actually do for a small business?

A marketing agency does outside work meant to bring a business more customers: its website, being found on Google and in AI answers, ads, social media, the handling of new inquiries, or several of these at once. What matters to an owner is what it hands over: a plan in plain words, a dated record of the work, accounts kept in the business's name, and a monthly count of inquiries by source. Choose the kind by the problem you have.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-does-a-marketing-agency-do/

### How can you tell whether your SEO agency is actually doing anything?

Check what you can see without knowing the technique. A working SEO agency can give you a dated list of what it changed and published, which you can confirm through logins held in your own name. Over quarters, more inquiries should arrive from search, each tagged with its source and followed to won, lost or still open. If a month shows nothing, ask what was done, what changed and what comes next, and expect a plain answer.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-tell-if-your-seo-agency-is-working/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### Can you turn off Google reviews for your business?

Not as an owner. Google's help page on managing reviews, as of October 2026, covers reading, replying to and reporting reviews, with no setting to turn them off. Google itself may temporarily disable reviews for certain profiles or business categories. Removing the profile does not clear them either: Google says reviews remain, while the owners' replies are permanently removed. What works instead is replying calmly, reporting reviews that break Google's policies and asking every customer for one.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-turn-off-google-reviews/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474050 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/10313341 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/14114287 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4669092 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3098204 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4596773 ; https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114

### Can you remove or turn off reviews on your Facebook business page?

Yes, a Facebook Page can switch them off as a whole. Meta's help page says turning Recommendations off "will disable Recommendations and remove the rating and reviews from your Page". The setting sits in the Page's Settings, under Page and tagging. To get a single recommendation taken down, Meta's route is to report it for breaking its Community Standards. On Facebook, a review is a recommendation: the customer picks Yes or No and writes a recommendation.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-remove-or-turn-off-facebook-reviews/
Sources: https://www.facebook.com/help/548274415377576 ; https://www.facebook.com/help/664755856965602 ; https://www.facebook.com/help/500762053364226 ; https://www.facebook.com/help/439579999521224

### What should you tell a marketing agency before it starts?

Before any work starts, give the agency a one-page brief: what you sell and to whom, the areas you serve, what a typical customer is worth to you, what has worked and what has not, where inquiries come from today, what you will and will not do yourself, and who approves work. A clear brief can save weeks of guessing, and it gives both sides something to judge the work against later.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-to-tell-a-marketing-agency-before-it-starts/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### Google Workspace or Microsoft 365: which should a small business use for email?

Both can give a small business email at its own domain, plus online file storage, document tools and video meetings, and both sell business plans for up to 300 users. The choice usually comes down to what your team already works in: Word and Excel files point toward Microsoft 365, Gmail and Google Docs toward Google Workspace. Whichever you pick, check that the plan includes email, set it up in the business's name, and make sure a second person can get in if the main admin is locked out.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/google-workspace-or-microsoft-365-for-business-email/
Sources: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/getting-started/editions/compare-business-editions ; https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/security-best-practices-for-administrator-accounts ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/office-365-plan-options ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/exchange-online-service-description/exchange-online-service-description ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/onedrive-for-business-service-description ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/teams-service-description ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/setup/setup-business-basic ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/add-users/about-admin-roles

### How do you work out who your target customer is?

Start from the jobs you already win and would happily take again, not from everyone who might buy. Look back over your recent customers and note what the good ones share: where they are, the type of job, how urgent it was and how they found you. Write the pattern down in a sentence or two. The SBA's market research questions, such as demand, location and how many similar options already exist, help you get a sense of the market for it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-find-your-target-customer/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/counseling/plan-your-business/

### What should a business email signature include?

A business email signature needs only the lines that help the reader act: your name and role, the business name, one phone number that reaches a person, the website and the area you serve. Hours or a usual reply time can help too. Leave out long quotes, banners and rows of icons, keep the phone number as text rather than inside an image, and use the same layout for everyone on the team.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-a-business-email-signature-include/

### Is Meta Verified worth it for a business?

Meta Verified for businesses is a paid subscription for a Facebook business Page, an Instagram professional business profile or a WhatsApp business profile. Meta says it comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support and impersonation protection. It can be worth it when people are copying your business, or when a locked account would cost you customers and you need help fast. On its own it is unlikely to bring new customers, so judge it by those risks rather than by reach.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-meta-verified-worth-it-for-a-business/
Sources: https://www.facebook.com/business/tools/meta-verified-for-business ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/308979828303560 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/help/248456111431653

### How do you cut spam calls to your business line without missing real customers?

Filter the calls your phone or carrier already flags as likely spam, but avoid settings that silence every unknown number: on a business line, new customers are usually unknown numbers. Screening, where the phone asks a caller who they are before it rings, is a safer middle ground. Do not count on the national Do Not Call registry for a business line: the FCC's rule protects registered residential subscribers, and the FTC's telemarketing rule exempts calls to businesses, with some exceptions. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-stop-spam-calls-to-your-business/
Sources: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/screen-and-block-calls-iphe4b3f7823/ios ; https://support.google.com/phoneapp/answer/3459196 ; https://support.google.com/phoneapp/answer/9118387 ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/47/64.1200 ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/310.6

### How should a service business respond to a customer complaint?

Reply the same day if you can, and listen to the whole complaint before offering a fix. Then make one clear offer you can keep, say when it will happen, and confirm it in writing. Do what you said, check back, and log the complaint and how it ended, because patterns show what to fix. Handled early and privately, a complaint often never turns into a public review.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-respond-to-a-customer-complaint/

### Should your marketing build brand awareness or bring in leads?

Most small service businesses should start with work that brings in leads they can trace, because it usually pays back sooner and shows what is working. Brand awareness, meaning how many people in your area know and remember your name, still matters: it feeds word of mouth, helps in a new area and can make every other channel work a little better. Add it once inquiries arrive steadily, and judge it by whether more people come to you by name.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/brand-awareness-or-leads/

### What is a unique selling proposition, and does a service business need one?

A unique selling proposition is the main reason a customer should choose you over the other businesses they are comparing, said in a sentence they could repeat to someone else. A service business usually benefits from one, because customers often compare a few options in minutes. The strongest come from what you already do and can show, such as how fast you respond, a specialty or an area you know well, not from words like quality that anyone can claim.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-unique-selling-proposition/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/counseling/plan-your-business/

### What should an owner look at in Google Analytics, and what can you ignore?

Once a month, look at four things: how many sessions the site had compared with earlier months, which channels they came from, which pages people landed on, and, if the site counts them, how many inquiries each channel and page produced. Google describes a session as a period of time during which a user interacts with your site. Most other reports, and day-to-day swings, can usually be left alone.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-an-owner-look-at-in-google-analytics/
Sources: https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9191807 ; https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9267568 ; https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9212670

### Can you see who visits your website?

Not by name. Website analytics shows counts and patterns: how many visits, which pages, where visitors came from and roughly where they are. It does not tell you who a visitor is, and Google's policies for Google Analytics say no data may be passed to Google that it could use or recognize as personally identifiable, such as an email address. Tools that claim to name visitors raise privacy questions. A visitor tells you who they are by getting in touch.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-see-who-visits-your-website/
Sources: https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/6366371

### What is domain authority, and should you pay an agency to raise it?

Domain Authority is a score from the SEO tool company Moz, not from Google. Moz describes it as a 1 to 100 score that compares how likely websites are to rank, and says it is not a Google ranking factor. Google says third-party SEO tools do not have access to its internal ranking data. A higher score is not a business result: judge an agency by the inquiries and customers that arrive from search.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/does-domain-authority-matter/
Sources: https://moz.com/learn/seo/domain-authority ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/third-party-seo ; https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/ranking-results/

### Can customers book an appointment with you straight from Google?

Often, yes. Google's Business Profile help describes two ways: add your own booking link, which sends customers to a page where they can book, or take bookings through a provider that works with Reserve with Google. Google says a business must be verified before it can add a link, not every business is eligible, and a provider might charge you. Whichever you use, record each booking as a lead with its source.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-customers-book-you-from-google/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/6218037 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/7475773 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/13769188 ; https://www.google.com/maps/reserve/

### Should you use AI to write your replies to reviews?

AI can help with a first draft, but a person who knows the job should edit and post every reply. AI was not there, can state wrong details with confidence and can repeat itself, and Google's own reply tips advise against sending everyone the same thank-you. Google now offers drafting itself: its help page says Gemini can draft review replies once an eligible owner connects the Business Profile.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-use-ai-to-reply-to-reviews/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474050 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/17142585

### Can a business stop customers from posting bad reviews?

Not with a standard contract term. The FTC's business guidance says the Consumer Review Fairness Act makes it illegal for a company to use a standard contract term that bars or restricts honest reviews, charges a penalty or fee for one, or makes reviewers give up intellectual property rights in their reviews. A business can still remove some content it hosts, report reviews that break a site's rules and reply. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-a-business-stop-bad-reviews/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-review-fairness-act-what-businesses-need-know ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122

### Will a new website or a new domain name hurt how you show up on Google?

It can, for a while, and much of the risk is avoidable. Google says that changing the addresses of existing pages can cause ranking fluctuations, and that a medium-sized site can take a few weeks for Google to notice the change. A new domain changes every address at once. Keep the domain if you can, keep the pages that bring visitors, make sure every old address leads to its new page, and compare inquiries before and after.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/will-a-new-website-or-domain-hurt-your-google-results/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/monitor-debug/debugging-search-traffic-drops ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/seo-starter-guide

### Which matter more for a service business: Google reviews or Yelp reviews?

For most service businesses, Google usually deserves the review request, because Google lets you ask customers for reviews and shows them next to your Business Profile in Maps and Search. Yelp says businesses should not ask anyone for reviews, and its star rating counts only the reviews its software recommends. So ask every customer for a Google review, keep your Yelp page claimed and answered, and let Yelp reviews arrive on their own.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/google-reviews-or-yelp-reviews/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/16816815 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4801187 ; https://www.yelp-support.com/article/Don-t-Ask-for-Reviews?l=en_US ; https://trust.yelp.com/recommendation-software/ ; https://blog.yelp.com/businesses/how-to-get-yelp-reviews-without-asking/ ; https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/

### Why can't you reply to a Google review?

Usually the profile or the account is the reason, not the review. Google says you must verify the business before you can reply, and you need to be signed in to a Google Account that owns or manages the profile. A reply that does not appear may still be in Google's check, which usually takes up to 10 minutes and sometimes up to 30 days. A review Google removed for breaking its policies is not restored.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-cant-you-reply-to-a-google-review/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474050 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/7107242 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3403100 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/10313341 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/10286840 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/14114287

### Can you get your home address or personal phone number out of Google results?

Often, yes. Google's "Results about you" tool finds search results that show your home address, phone number or email and lets you ask Google to remove them. It removes the result from Google Search, not the page, so the details stay on the website itself. Google says it offers no removal for some sites it treats as valuable to the public, such as government sites, newspapers and business websites, or for details you control yourself.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/remove-your-home-address-or-phone-from-google/
Sources: https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/12719076 ; https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/9673730 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/2853879

### What is a Google Local Guide, and do their reviews count for more?

A Local Guide is a member of Google's Local Guides program, a community of individuals who contribute reviews, photos, edits and facts to Google Maps; each contribution earns points, and from Level 4, at 250 points, Google shows a Local Guide badge. Google says the badge helps contributions get noticed, while its review score is the average of all ratings published on Google. Treat a guide's review like any other, and never offer a guide anything: Google says "Soliciting Local Guides is strictly prohibited".

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-google-local-guide/
Sources: https://support.google.com/maps/answer/6225846 ; https://support.google.com/maps/answer/6225851 ; https://support.google.com/maps/answer/10287202 ; https://support.google.com/maps/answer/7358351 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4801187 ; https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114

### What is a large language model (LLM), in plain terms?

A large language model, or LLM, is software trained on a huge amount of text to predict which words are likely to come next, which lets it write, summarize and answer questions in plain language. LLMs are the basis of chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. Because an LLM predicts likely wording rather than looking facts up, it can sound certain and still be wrong, and the same question can get a different answer each time.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-large-language-model/
Sources: https://cloud.google.com/ai/llms ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model ; https://gemini.google/overview/ ; https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/llm/transformers

### Is a Wix or Squarespace website bad for showing up on Google?

Usually not. Google's starter guide names no website builder and says that, for Google to find a site, you usually don't need to do anything except publish it. Wix says its sites are designed to be search engine friendly on any plan, and Squarespace says the content you add and how you present it play a big role in how well people find you. The limits owners tend to hit are control, speed and moving out.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-a-wix-or-squarespace-site-bad-for-google/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/seo-starter-guide ; https://support.wix.com/en/article/search-engine-optimization-seo ; https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/360002090267-SEO-checklist

### What should you do about duplicate Google listings or a second Google profile for your business?

First work out whether it is a true duplicate. Google allows one Business Profile per business and says a duplicate will not show on Search or Maps, but a second location with its own staff and service area, or a distinct business at your address, can have its own. A copy you made by mistake can be removed by its owner, and two Maps listings for one business can be reported for a merge, which Google reviews.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-merge-or-remove-duplicate-google-listings/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/12756178 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4669092 ; https://support.google.com/maps/answer/10552932

### How should a business reply to a positive Google review?

Keep it short and specific. Thank the customer, mention one real detail of the job, and stop there. Google's reply tips say to be conversational, not promotional: skip deals and promotions, and share "a detail that reinforces their experience and encourages a return visit". Write each reply fresh rather than pasting one thank-you everywhere, leave out private details, and never offer anything in return for a review.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-reply-to-a-positive-google-review/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474050

### Can you give customers a discount or a gift for leaving a review?

No. Google's Maps content policy bars businesses from offering incentives, such as payment, discounts or free goods or services, in exchange for posting any review. The FTC says its review rule separately bans incentives conditioned, openly or by implication, on a positive or negative review, and that failing to disclose other incentives could violate the FTC Act. As general advice, offer nothing for any review, anywhere, and ask every customer the same way. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-give-customers-a-discount-for-a-review/
Sources: https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/14114287 ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers

### What should a marketing agency contract say before you sign it?

Before signing, check that the contract says in plain words what work is included, how long it runs and whether it renews automatically, how and when either side can end it, that your accounts, content and data stay in your business's name, what reports you get, how your information is kept confidential, and what you receive back when it ends. If any of those is missing or vague, ask for it in writing first.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-a-marketing-agency-contract-include/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/scams-your-small-business-guide-business

### Should a service business put its time into SEO or into social media?

For most service businesses, the first hours are usually best spent on being found where customers check before they hire: Google search, the map results and AI answers. Those people need the job done now. Social media mostly reaches people who are not looking yet, which can build familiarity and referrals but often brings work more slowly. Once search is covered, add one social platform your customers use, and judge both by the inquiries each brings in.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/seo-or-social-media-for-a-service-business/
Sources: https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/social-media/ ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### Why do Google results look different on your phone than on a customer's?

Because Google tailors results to the person and the moment. Google says it uses information such as your location, past Search history and Search settings, and results also vary with time, language and device. An owner searching from the shop, signed in, after many visits to their own site, may see the business higher than a customer across town does. For a fairer picture, search signed out, from other places and on other people's phones.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-google-results-look-different-for-you-and-your-customers/
Sources: https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/12412910?hl=en ; https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/179386?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop ; https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/ranking-results/

### What is a marketing audit, and is it worth paying for?

A marketing audit is a review of everything a business does to win and handle customers: the website, Google profile, reviews, social pages, ads, email and how inquiries are answered. A worthwhile one hands the owner a plain list of what exists, what works, what is missing and what to do first, with a reason for each. It is usually worth paying for when you could act on it without hiring the person who wrote it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-is-a-marketing-audit/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/do-i-need-seo

### Is it safe to put customer information into ChatGPT or another AI tool?

Usually not without care. What you type into an AI chat tool usually goes to the company that runs it, and its terms and settings decide how it is kept and used. The U.S. Small Business Administration advises trying not to feed AI tools sensitive data. As a default, leave out payment, health and account details, and names or contact details unless the task needs them. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-put-customer-information-into-chatgpt/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/manage-your-business/ai-small-business ; https://www.ftc.gov/policy/advocacy-research/tech-at-ftc/2024/01/ai-companies-uphold-your-privacy-confidentiality-commitments ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/protecting-personal-information-guide-business

### What can a small business safely use AI for in its marketing?

AI is usually safe for drafts, ideas, summaries and tidying your own words, as long as a person checks the result before customers see it. It is risky for facts, prices, claims, review replies and anything holding customer details. Handing it the owner's own conversations with customers is usually not worth it yet. The U.S. Small Business Administration advises starting small and having a person assess every message and outreach campaign that AI generates.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-can-a-small-business-use-ai-for-in-marketing/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/manage-your-business/ai-small-business ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content

### How do ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google's AI answers, Gemini, Copilot and Claude find local businesses?

ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, Gemini, Copilot and Claude all say they can draw on the live web and show links or citations, with conditions that vary by plan and setting. Of the platform pages read on 2026-10-24, only Google's describe a listing a business can claim: its Business Profile. The others describe no way for a business to add or claim a listing. No platform is ranked here.
