### Is radio, TV or billboard advertising worth it for a service business?

Sometimes. Radio, TV and billboard ads can reach a whole area at once, so they can suit a service business with a wide service area, a service most households need sooner or later, and room for more work. They are hard to trace, because many people who hear or see them get in touch days later, often by searching your name. Give the ad its own phone number or short web address, ask every new customer how they heard of you, and judge the run by jobs won.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-radio-tv-or-billboard-advertising-worth-it/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/

### Should a local business pay influencers, and what do they have to disclose?

Paying a local creator can make sense when a creator's followers are mostly people in your area who could hire you. The Federal Trade Commission's Endorsement Guides, its interpretation of the laws it enforces, say a payment, a free or discounted service or another benefit can be a connection that must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously when it could materially affect how much weight followers give the post and they would not expect it. They say the business can be liable too. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-pay-influencers-to-promote-your-business/
Sources: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/255.0 ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/255.1 ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/255.5

### What should a simple marketing plan for a service business include?

A simple marketing plan for a service business fits on one page. It names the customers you want and the area you serve, why they should choose you, the few channels you will use and what each should bring in, what you will spend, who does the work, and the date you check the results. Most of these match sections the U.S. Small Business Administration suggests, and it says a marketing plan should be maintained at least once a year.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-should-a-small-business-marketing-plan-include/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/

### How should a small business decide how much to spend on marketing?

Set the budget from your own numbers. Work out what a new customer is worth and how much of that you would spend to win one, then how many new jobs you want and how many inquiries that takes. Put most of the money into channels your records show bring jobs at that cost, keep a smaller fixed amount to test one new channel with an end date, count your own hours as well as money, and adjust after each review.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-much-should-a-small-business-spend-on-marketing/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/

### Why did my Google or Facebook ads stop working?

First work out which problem you have. If the ads stopped running, the cause is usually in the ad account: Google's help pages list a paused, ended or removed ad, a disapproved ad, a budget that limits the campaign, and missing or invalid billing information among the reasons. If the ads still run but stopped bringing inquiries, look at what happens after the click: the page, the form, the phone, your reply time, the season and competitors. Hold off on raising the budget until you know which.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-did-my-google-or-facebook-ads-stop-working/
Sources: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7378077 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722129

### Will AI replace marketing agencies, and do you still need one?

No one can say for certain how far AI will change marketing work. AI tools can already help with drafts, summaries and first checks, while knowing the business, checking facts and answering for results usually still need a person. So the useful question for an owner is how an agency uses AI: which parts it hands to a tool, who checks the output, and what it can actually show you.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/will-ai-replace-marketing-agencies/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/manage-your-business/ai-small-business ; https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/08/ftc-finalizes-orders-cox-media-group-two-other-firms-settling-charges-they-deceived-customers-about

### Can you use AI to write reviews or testimonials for your business?

No. The FTC says its rule on consumer reviews and testimonials, in effect since October 21, 2024, bars businesses from creating or selling reviews or testimonials that falsely claim to come from someone who does not exist, such as AI-generated fake reviews, or from someone with no actual experience of the business. Google's Maps policy also removes content not based on a real experience. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-use-ai-to-write-reviews-or-testimonials/
Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2024/08/federal-trade-commission-announces-final-rule-banning-fake-reviews-testimonials ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/blog/2025/12/warning-letter-or-ten-businesses-comply-ftcs-consumer-review-rule ; https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/12/ftc-reopens-sets-aside-rytr-final-order-response-trump-administrations-ai-action-plan ; https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114

### Do you have to tell customers when you use AI to answer or write to them?

It depends on the state and the use. The U.S. Small Business Administration's guide says no federal or state laws currently require businesses to disclose AI use, and that disclosure is becoming an expected best practice. Utah's code, though, requires a supplier whose generative AI interacts with a person in a consumer transaction to say so when the person clearly asks. As general advice, tell customers plainly anyway. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/do-you-have-to-tell-customers-you-use-ai/
Sources: https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/manage-your-business/ai-small-business ; https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title13/Chapter77/C13-77-S103_2025050720250507.html ; https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title13/Chapter77/C13-77-S104_2025050720250507.html ; https://www.pewresearch.org/science/2025/09/17/how-americans-view-ai-and-its-impact-on-people-and-society/ ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content

### What happens to your website, Google profile, phone number and reviews when you sell a business?

Usually only what the sale agreement lists, and only once each account is actually handed over. The domain, website and hosting, Google Business Profile, ad accounts, social pages, business phone number and customer records usually each sit in a separate account with its own handover. Google says transferring primary ownership of the profile to the new owner keeps its information, such as reviews. List every account before either side signs. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-goes-with-your-business-when-you-sell-or-buy-it-online/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3415281 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3098204 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 ; https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/manage-your-business/close-or-sell-your-business

### What is the difference between SEO and SEM?

SEO, search engine optimization, is work aimed at being found in the unpaid search results. SEM, search engine marketing, is used loosely: it often means paid search ads, and some sellers use it for paid and unpaid search work together. With paid search ads you usually pay for each click on an ad shown in a labeled ad spot, and Google says no one can buy a better place in its unpaid results. Because the label varies, ask any seller exactly what SEM includes.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/seo-or-sem-whats-the-difference/
Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/seo-starter-guide ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/116495 ; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722047 ; https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/our-approach/ads-on-search/

### Should you delete your Google Business Profile and start over?

Usually not. Google's page on removing a Business Profile says the posts, photos and review replies of its owners and managers are permanently removed, while customer reviews remain and the business might still show on Search and Maps. Removal fits a copy you created by mistake. For a closure, a sale, a move or a suspension, Google's pages point to a better route, and a fresh profile for the same business can end up treated as a duplicate.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/should-you-delete-your-google-business-profile/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/4669092 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/16043467 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/15300196 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3415281 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3098204 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4569145 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/12756178

### Can an online-only business have a Google Business Profile?

Usually not. Google's eligibility guidelines say a business must make in-person contact with customers during its stated hours, and they list online-only businesses among the examples that are not eligible. A business that travels to customers can still qualify as a service-area business, with its address hidden. One that deals with customers only online is usually better served by its own website and by being easy to describe wherever customers look it up.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-an-online-only-business-have-a-google-business-profile/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/13763036 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4569145

### Can customers leave a Google review without a Gmail account?

Yes, as long as they have a Google Account. Google's tips for getting reviews say customers must be signed in to a Google Account to leave a review, and that they can set one up with a non-Gmail email address. There is no anonymous option: Google's Maps help says all reviews are public. Tell customers that plainly, send a direct link, and never offer anything in return for the review.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-customers-review-you-without-a-gmail-account/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/16816815 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/10313341 ; https://support.google.com/maps/answer/6230175 ; https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114

### Why is your business pin in the wrong place on Google Maps, and how do you fix it?

Google says it decides how to show a business's address from the owner's information and other sources, and lets an owner pin the location directly when the address has no street number or cannot be found. To move the pin, open your Business Profile, select Edit profile, then Location, Edit next to Business location, then Adjust; move the map and save. Google reviews the change, which usually takes about 10 minutes and can take up to 30 days.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/why-is-your-business-in-the-wrong-place-on-google-maps/

### How does Google work out your star rating, and do old reviews ever expire?

Google says the review score is the average of all ratings published on Google for the business, on a scale of one to five stars, and that a new review can take up to 2 weeks to show in it. On old reviews, Google's Maps help tells reviewers that a review shows up until they take it down, and names no expiry. The score moves when ratings are added, edited, deleted or removed, and a profile with few ratings moves the most.

### How do you get your business on Apple Maps, and is it worth it?

Claim your location through Apple Business, the free Apple service that replaced Apple Business Connect in April 2026. Once your location is verified, you manage the place card customers see in Apple Maps: name, hours, phone, website, photos and a short description. Apple says place cards also appear in Siri, Spotlight and other Apple apps. For a business people look up or drive to, it is usually worth claiming.

### Can you remove photos from your Google Business Profile, including ones customers posted?

Yes for photos you added, and only sometimes for customers' photos. Google lets an owner delete photos and videos the owner uploaded to the Business Profile. Photos posted by customers are different: Google says you can't stop customers posting photo updates, but you can report a photo or video that breaks its policies. Google then reviews it, which can take several business days, and may or may not remove it. A photo that is simply unflattering usually stays.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/remove-photos-from-your-google-business-profile/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/6103862 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/9867764 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/6130451

### Are those 'your business has won an award' emails legit?

Some are real, but many are vanity awards: an email says your business has won, then asks for a fee to claim a plaque, certificate or promotion. The Better Business Bureau says most legitimate awards cost the recipient nothing, and that if you did not apply, or the sender cannot say how you were nominated, the award is probably not legitimate. Before paying anything, ask who chose you and how, look the company up, and do not click the email's links.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/are-business-award-emails-legit/
Sources: https://www.bbb.org/article/business/21031-bbb-tip-vanity-awards ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/scams-your-small-business-guide-business

### Is Trustpilot worth it for a local service business?

Usually not as a first priority. Trustpilot lets a business claim its profile, reply to reviews and invite customers for free, and sells paid plans with extra tools. It tends to suit businesses that sell online; customers of local service businesses usually read Google reviews first. Claim your profile if customers already review you there, invite everyone the same way with no incentives, and pay for a plan only if your records show customers using it.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/is-trustpilot-worth-it-for-a-service-business/
Sources: https://corporate.trustpilot.com/trust ; https://corporate.trustpilot.com/legal/for-businesses/guidelines-for-businesses/sep-2026 ; https://business.trustpilot.com/pricing ; https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/

### How do you get your business on Waze?

Your business may already be on Waze: Waze says the business details it shows come from Waze users, Google and other partners. If it is missing, anyone can suggest it as a place in the Waze app, and Waze's volunteer map editors review it before it goes on the map. Paid pins are separate: Google says U.S. businesses can now appear as promoted pins on Waze through some Google Ads campaigns. Waze usually matters most for businesses customers drive to.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-to-get-your-business-on-waze/
Sources: https://support.google.com/waze/answer/11942300 ; https://support.google.com/waze/answer/6262592 ; https://support.google.com/waze/answer/6263233 ; https://support.google.com/wazeads/answer/14260169 ; https://business.google.com/us/accelerate/announcements/access-new-inventory-and-channel-performance-reporting-in-performance-max-campaigns/

### Can you find out who left a Google review?

Only what the reviewer's public profile shows. Google's Maps help says all reviews are public and none can be anonymous, so you see the name on the reviewer's About me page and their other public reviews and photos. Google's privacy policy says it does not share personal information with individuals outside Google except in cases it lists, such as consent or legal reasons. If the name fits no customer, check your records, reply calmly and report the review if it breaks Google's rules.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/can-you-find-out-who-left-a-google-review/
Sources: https://support.google.com/maps/answer/6230175 ; https://policies.google.com/privacy ; https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/4596773 ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers

### How do you get outdated or wrong information about your business off Google Search?

Start with the site that published it, because Google does not own other websites. Google's help says to contact the website owner, and that even when Google drops a result, the page itself is still there. Once the site's owner removes the old information, Google says it eventually leaves its results through regular updating, and Google offers a request to refresh an outdated result. Wrong details on your own Google Business Profile are a separate fix.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/remove-outdated-information-from-google/
Sources: https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/9109 ; https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/6349986 ; https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/2744324

### What is a Google knowledge panel, and is it different from a Business Profile?

A knowledge panel is an information box Google generates automatically for people, places, organizations and things it recognizes, drawing on sources across the web. A Business Profile looks similar but, Google says, is specific to businesses that serve customers at a location or within a service area, and the business claims or creates it. For a local service business, the box customers see is usually its Business Profile. Google says it does not manually create or delete knowledge panels, so treat anyone selling one with caution.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/knowledge-panel-or-business-profile/
Sources: https://support.google.com/knowledgepanel/answer/9163198 ; https://support.google.com/knowledgepanel/answer/7534902 ; https://support.google.com/knowledgepanel/answer/7534842 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/2721884

### What are AI browsers, and do they change how customers find a business?

An AI browser is a web browser with an AI assistant built in, so a person can ask questions about the pages they have open, compare them and, in some, hand over tasks. Perplexity's Comet uses Perplexity's AI search as its primary search engine; Google offers Gemini in Chrome, and Microsoft offers Copilot in Edge. For a business, it may mean a customer compares your site with others in one request. No source cited here measures how many customers use them.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/what-are-ai-browsers/
Sources: https://www.perplexity.ai/comet ; https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/introducing-comet ; https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/11172798-getting-started-with-comet ; https://www.google.com/chrome/ai-innovations/ ; https://gemini.google/overview/gemini-in-chrome/ ; https://explore.microsoft.com/en-us/edge/copilot

### Why does a competitor's ad show up when people search my business name?

Because Google's ad rules allow it. Google's trademark policy says it will not restrict using trademarks as keywords, the search words an advertiser picks. On a trademark owner's complaint, it may restrict a direct competitor using the trademark in the ad text, or an ad that uses it in a confusing, deceptive or misleading way. The ad does not buy better placement in the unpaid results. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/competitor-ads-on-your-business-name/
Sources: https://support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/6118 ; https://support.google.com/adspolicy/troubleshooter/14327740 ; https://support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/6020955 ; https://support.google.com/My-Ad-Center-Help/answer/13861201 ; https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/our-approach/ads-on-search/

### How do photographers get clients?

Photographers usually get clients by showing the work where people look at pictures, then making it easy to ask. A portfolio page for each kind of work, an Instagram and Pinterest presence, a Google profile with a home address hidden, and an inquiry form that asks the date and venue first are a good start. There is no fast route; most of it builds slowly.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-do-photographers-get-clients/
Sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 ; https://www.facebook.com/business/instagram/getting-started ; https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/pin-performance-and-distribution

### How do accountants and bookkeepers get clients?

Accountants and bookkeepers usually get clients through referrals first, then through directories a buyer may check, such as a state CPA society, QuickBooks ProAdvisor and Xero. Tax season changes what a website should offer. In Florida, the statute bars knowingly using the title CPA without an active license or practice privileges. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-do-accountants-get-clients/
Sources: https://www.ficpa.org/find-a-firm ; https://quickbooks.intuit.com/find-an-accountant ; https://www.xero.com/us/advisors/ ; https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224841 ; https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/473.322

### How do plumbers get more leads?

Plumbers usually get more leads by answering the emergency call, because an urgent customer often takes whoever replies first. Local Services Ads are one paid option; a complete Google profile, past customers and fairly asked reviews cost only time. In Florida, the statute puts a contractor's license number in offers and advertisements. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-do-plumbers-get-more-leads/
Sources: https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224841 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 ; https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481 ; https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/489.119 ; https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/489.105

### How do HVAC companies get leads?

HVAC companies usually get leads from demand that follows the weather, so the work is to be easy to find and easy to choose when it arrives. That means Google Local Services Ads where eligible, a maintenance-plan page that works between seasons, manufacturer dealer-locator listings, and any lead company judged by booked jobs. Commercial work is a different buyer, often asking for bids rather than calls.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-do-hvac-companies-get-leads/
Sources: https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224841 ; https://www.trane.com/residential/en/dealer-locator/

### How do personal trainers and fitness coaches get clients online?

Personal trainers and fitness coaches usually get clients online by being found on Instagram and converting on a website: a page for each kind of client, a short next step, and public claims that do not promise results. In the FTC's view, objective product claims need adequate substantiation, and its health-products guidance covers products, not coaching as such. This is a plain summary, not legal advice.

Full answer: https://ascentvision.org/answers/how-do-personal-trainers-get-clients-online/
Sources: https://www.facebook.com/business/instagram/getting-started ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/health-products-compliance-guidance ; https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224841

## Calculators

### Marketing ROI calculator

This calculator turns five numbers you already have (what you spent on marketing in a period, the inquiries it brought, the share you won, your average job value and your margin) into cost per inquiry, cost per customer, gross and net return, margin earned per dollar spent and the close rate at which the spend breaks even. It is arithmetic on your own numbers, not a forecast, and the numbers you type are not stored or sent anywhere.

Calculator: https://ascentvision.org/tools/marketing-roi-calculator/

### Customer lifetime value calculator

This calculator works out what a typical customer is worth over the time they stay with you: average sale times purchases a year times years, with your margin applied and, if you want, one round of referrals. From that it gives the most you can spend to win one customer at a target return you choose, and what that allows per inquiry at your close rate. It is arithmetic on your own numbers, not a forecast, and the numbers you type are not stored or sent anywhere.

Calculator: https://ascentvision.org/tools/customer-lifetime-value-calculator/

### How many inquiries do you need? A calculator

This calculator works backwards from a monthly goal. A revenue goal divided by your average job value gives the jobs you need; dividing by your close rate gives the appointments or quotes that must happen; dividing by your show rate gives the inquiries you need each month and each week. Add the inquiries each channel brings today and it shows the gap. It is arithmetic on your own numbers, not a forecast, and the numbers you type are not stored or sent anywhere.

Calculator: https://ascentvision.org/tools/how-many-inquiries-do-you-need/
Sources: https://hbr.org/2011/03/the-short-life-of-online-sales-leads ; https://www.smartcompany.com.au/marketing/20110704-are-you-letting-online-leads-go-cold/

## Research

### What 96 Florida service-business websites leave out

On October 24, 2026, Ascent Vision read the public pages of 96 small Florida service-business websites in 10 regions (the home page and up to 6 more pages each). 64 of 96 (67%) did not say, in the first lines of the home page, all three of what the business does, where it works and who it is for; 51 of 96 (53%) left out who it is for and 28 of 96 (29%) left out where. 24 of 96 (25%) offered no way to get in touch on the home page itself, and 32 of 96 (33%) had no tap-to-call phone number on any page read. 29 of 96 (30%) gave search engines and AI assistants no machine-readable summary of the business, and 24 of 96 (25%) had no summary line written for search results.

Full page, with every count and its N: https://ascentvision.org/research/florida-service-business-websites-2026/

## Questions and answers

### What does Ascent Vision do?

Ascent Vision is a Florida marketing company for small service businesses and independent professionals. It makes them visible on Google and in AI answers (SEO and GEO), generates and tracks leads through lead systems that turn those visits into inquiries, and upgrades or builds the website they run on. Every lead is tracked back to where it came from.

### Is Ascent Vision the same company as Ascent Vision Technologies or CACI Ascent Vision?

No. Ascent Vision LLC is a Florida marketing company founded in 2026 by Clayton Camera and Grayson Sorrentino. CACI Ascent Vision, LLC (formerly Ascent Vision Technologies) is a Montana imaging and counter-drone company, owned by CACI International since 2020, that does business as "Ascent Vision" in federal contracting records. The two have never been connected.

### What is GEO?

GEO, generative engine optimization, is the work of making a business the one AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI answers recommend when a customer asks them who to call. People now ask assistants as well as search engines, so being part of that answer matters alongside ranking.

### How is GEO different from SEO?

SEO aims for a ranked link on a search results page. GEO aims for a mention or recommendation inside an AI-written answer. The two support each other, and Ascent Vision measures them separately, because a business that ranks is not always the business an assistant recommends.

### How do I know what the work produced?

Every lead from an Ascent Vision site or campaign is recorded with where it came from, such as a search, an AI answer, a referral or an ad, so a client can see which leads the work produced and what happened to each one.

### Do you publish prices?

No. Every engagement is scoped on a call first, because the work depends on the business, the market and what already exists. Start with the application on the Work with us page: nine short questions, about two minutes.

### Can I meet Ascent Vision in person?

Yes. Most of Ascent Vision's meetings are by video call, and clients near Tallahassee, Florida, can also meet the founders in person by appointment.

### Who does Ascent Vision work with?

Ascent Vision works with small businesses and independent professionals who sell a service and want more of their customers to find them through search and AI answers. Its first client is an online fitness coaching business.

### Who owns the website and the content?

The client owns their domain, their content and their lead data. Ascent Vision builds and runs the work; it does not hold a client's site or customers hostage.
